Aspects of French-speaking Society: Current Trends — a core area of A-Level French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: How many députés sit in the Assemblée nationale?
When does the past participle agree with avoir verbs?
options: Always.
Either position with the same meaning.
When the direct object comes BEFORE the verb (la pomme que j'ai mangée).
Never - avoir never causes agreement.
Actually (in reality).
Either position with the same meaning.
Currently/at the moment.
Annually.

mcqs.q: Where does 'petit' usually go in relation to its noun?
options: Annually.
Either position with the same meaning.
Before the noun (un petit garçon).
After the noun like most French adjectives.
